# Lab notebook {#sec-notebook}

::: {.callout-important title="Research ledger, not execution diary"}
This notebook records questions, discriminating evidence, belief changes,
corrections, and research decisions. The contemporaneous full chronology was
archived on 2026-07-29 because it mixed scientific reasoning with execution
detail. The full record remains available in
`results/notebook_full_chronology_through_2026-07-29.qmd`; it is not part of
the scientific argument. Run mechanics, implementation notes, complete tables,
and debugging history belong with each experiment's result record. They enter
this ledger only when they change a scientific interpretation; such
corrections are marked **EDIT**.
:::

The entries below are a compact chronology. “Registered” means the comparison
and decision rule were written before its deciding measurements. “Exploratory”
means useful for hypothesis formation but not confirmation. “Invalid” means
the instrument could not answer the stated question; its numerical outputs
may remain observations, but the associated interpretation is withdrawn.

Iterations 1--6 predate this ledger and are summarized in @sec-learned-bie,
@sec-parametric, and @sec-3d-results.

## Current research agenda {#sec-nb-current-agenda}

The long-term question is whether a surrogate can map boundary conditions and
geometry to PDE-governed fields while transferring across discretization,
operator parameters, and geometry families. Current evidence does **not**
identify a universal architecture. It supports a research program with four
questions:

| Research question | What is known | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Which boundary and geometry information must be preserved? | Structured boundary propagation helps on controlled PDE families, but the necessary state under changing geometry is unknown. | Establish whether transfer exists first; analyze internal state only to explain a valid outcome. |
| Which physical priors help? | Several exact structures improved fidelity or efficiency; others were neutral, harmful, or invalidated by bugs. | Require a controlled transfer or scaling gain before promoting any prior into the architecture. |
| Can one learned model transfer between families? | Within-family transfer was sometimes good; untouched vehicle-family transfer failed decisively. | Industrial generalization remains unearned. |
| Is one architecture plausible at all? | Broad PDE pretraining makes reusable representations credible, but remote frozen-model transfer remains unproved. | Separate frozen transfer, few-shot adaptation, and design reuse; do not call all three “generality.” |

The validity triage in @sec-nb-validity-triage found no old run whose immediate
repetition can change this agenda. Geometry-family transfer remains first and
cross-regime transfer second. The latest self-contained program assessment is
@sec-nb-checkin-transfer-first; it supersedes recent attempts to make a
complete theory of interface state a prerequisite for the first transfer
verdict. The active scientific claim is condensed in
@sec-nb-geometry-transfer-claim-card. No experiment or compute is active.

## 2026-07-03 to 2026-07-05 — controlled representation studies {#sec-nb-controlled-program}

### Iteration 7 — a learned boundary kernel escapes finite moments {#sec-nb-iter7}

The kernel decoder broke the moment decoder's finite-mode nullspace and
improved under boundary refinement. The first measurement was single-seed and
preliminary, but later reference-bank studies preserved the qualitative
finding: pairwise boundary-to-query propagation is the useful abstraction,
not a small fixed set of global moments.

### Iteration 8 — nonlinear drive dependence is sometimes necessary {#sec-nb-iter8}

On Liouville, every exactly drive-linear model remained on the predicted
superposition wall. A zero-preserving nonlinear read-in crossed it at all
three seeds, while adding smooth learned kernel members did not help. This
established nonlinear drive interaction as a real representational need, but
not a license to use it on linear PDEs.

### Iteration 9 — screened Laplace, historical observation and correction {#sec-nb-iter9}

The generic kernel model degraded smoothly across screening values, whereas
the historical “Yukawa specialist” collapsed at low screening. Smooth learned
members again damaged extrapolation.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the specialist was not a valid boundary-integral
instrument: its trace normalization was inconsistent, a material
single-layer self term was absent, and its charged low-screening iteration was
unstable. The generic model's measured errors remain real, but the comparison
does **not** show an inherent failure of screened kernels.

### Iteration 10 — dimensional genericity held; the first mechanism story did not {#sec-nb-iter10}

The same architecture ran in three dimensions without a core change. An early
reading that smooth learned members became beneficial in 3D was later
overturned: their apparent benefit was compensation for a harmful polynomial
dictionary, not a dimension-dependent reversal.

### Iteration 11 — structured singular members beat a larger dictionary {#sec-nb-iter11}

A registered 2D ablation found that the singular-only dictionary matched or
beat singular-plus-polynomial and learned-member alternatives on
interpolation and frequency transfer. Polynomial and learned members could
interact destructively. More dictionary elements were not more expressive in
the sense that mattered for transfer.

### Iterations 12--13 — the dictionary result generalized, with one nonlinear exception {#sec-nb-iter12}

The 3D disentangler confirmed that polynomial members were harmful there too;
removing them reduced error and seed variance. Singular-only also remained
strong on screened Laplace. It failed on nonlinear Liouville, sharpening the
rule: use the smallest physically licensed dictionary that spans the
operator, and add learned smooth structure only when a falsifier shows the
span is insufficient.

### Iteration 14 — scalar channels are enough only on the easy 2D family {#sec-nb-iter14}

Scalar-only propagation matched the full typed model on 2D Laplace, even
after a capacity-matched control, but degraded on screened and 3D problems.
Vector channels therefore encode a cross-family requirement rather
than merely extra parameters.

### Iterations 15 and 17 — generic attention baselines did not close the gap {#sec-nb-iter15}

At matched resources in the streaming regime, Transolver was markedly worse
than the structured boundary model and violated similarity covariance.
Because that was not Transolver's native setting, the claim remained scoped
until the fixed-dataset comparison.

### Iteration 17 — the comparison remained the fixed-dataset regime {#sec-nb-iter17}

On a fixed FEM-labeled dataset, both matched-size and native-size Transolver
controls remained worse, including on trace-frequency transfer. This supports
the boundary-kernel inductive bias rather than a manufactured-label or
streaming-data artifact.

### Iteration 16 — adding a classical kernel member is not automatically helpful {#sec-nb-iter16}

A single-layer member failed its predicted topology benefit and damaged
frequency transfer. Free learned coefficients used its smooth far field to
absorb interpolation error. The lesson was not “single layers are bad,” but
that physically recognizable basis functions remain dangerous when their
coefficients are unconstrained by the boundary equation.

### Iterations 18--19 — nonlocal boundary processing is conditional {#sec-nb-iter18}

On all-Dirichlet problems, removing boundary self-attention was essentially
neutral. That null was predicted by the near-local second-kind trace
structure, not treated as universal.

### Iteration 19 — mixed conditions require one attention layer {#sec-nb-iter19}

The registered mixed-boundary discriminator made the zero-layer model
unreliable, while one and two layers were comparable. The compact conclusion
is one nonlocal boundary layer by default, with deeper processing requiring
new evidence.

### Iteration 20 — refinement transferred; dense pair cost did not {#sec-nb-iter20}

The model retained accuracy under a sixteenfold resolution change, supporting
a continuum rather than fixed-mesh interpretation. Dense boundary-query
propagation nevertheless scales quadratically in the two supports. That cost
motivates fast evaluation, but it is an implementation constraint rather than
evidence for a different surrogate mechanism.

### Iteration 21 — potential flow exposed a missing representation type {#sec-nb-iter21}

The first potential-flow formulation failed because circulation is a
pseudoscalar and the requested streamfunction/velocity transformations were
outside the model's declared type algebra. The failure was representational,
not an inability to learn exterior flow.

### Iteration 22 — representable targets removed the wall {#sec-nb-iter22}

Supplying the boundary trace produced strong interpolation and geometry
transfer. A velocity reformulation learned the potential component but left a
nearly constant circulation error, exactly where the missing pseudoscalar
product predicted. This was the discriminating evidence needed to extend the
type system.

### Iteration 23 — the pseudoscalar extension closed the prediction {#sec-nb-iter23}

Declaring 2D pseudoscalar channels and their closed products removed the
circulation wall across five seeds. This is one of the program's clearest
examples of a physics prior earning complexity: a structural impossibility
was identified before the extension, and the predicted component moved after
it.

### Iteration 24 — an intrinsic length gauge is theoretically preferable {#sec-nb-iter24}

Any degree-one geometric length preserves similarity covariance, so a
measure-weighted RMS radius can replace a caller-supplied reference length.
The theoretical statement remains. The later industrial calibration of its
constant did not satisfy its claimed train-only protocol and is treated
separately below.

### Iteration 25 — nonlinear output degree must be representable {#sec-nb-iter25}

Euler--Bernoulli pressure is even and quadratic in the drive, while an exactly
linear mode is drive-odd. The linear model therefore had a structural pressure
wall; a nonlinear mode crossed it. This generalized the Liouville lesson from
“nonlinearity may matter” to “the declared output degree must contain the
physics.”

### Iteration 26 — exact contracts help, but only when they are correct {#sec-nb-iter26}

The operator/drive stream split enforced zero-drive and superposition to
machine precision, whereas a free control learned only approximate versions.
It did not improve frequency extrapolation. More importantly, zero
preservation is wrong for Liouville's nonzero homogeneous solution. Exact
priors require a per-problem correctness check; exact enforcement can make a
misspecification worse.

### Iterations 27--30 — far-field decay needs its own structure {#sec-nb-iter27}

Coverage, member decay, and coefficient extrapolation were separated through
registered discriminators. Expanding the training annulus helped but did not
remove the gap, and simply adding smooth members did not fix it.

### Iteration 30 — licensed decay constraints helped but did not finish the problem {#sec-nb-iter30}

A direct-drive decay envelope and monopole-free deflation improved far-field
error consistently across five seeds, but did not reach the fully solved bar.
The remaining issue belongs to global exterior propagation, not the local
singularity.

### Iterations 31--32 — one full-width head is the parsimonious default {#sec-nb-iter31}

At fixed score capacity on Laplace, one head was more accurate and stable than
four or eight. The registered cross-suite check was needed before changing the
default.

### Iteration 32 — the cross-suite result was noninferiority, not superiority {#sec-nb-iter32}

One head matched the four-head model on every registered split across
screened, potential-flow, and 3D suites, but the Laplace accuracy gain did not
travel. The default changed on parsimony grounds, with a standing falsifier if
a later suite shows a decisive loss.

### Iteration 33 — rotational Euler opened an operator-parameter failure {#sec-nb-iter33}

Exact rotational Euler solutions showed reasonable interpolation but
catastrophic behavior near held-out spectral structure. The failure co-varied
with implicit nonlinear degree and operator resonance, motivating a direct
mechanism study rather than a larger sweep.

### Iteration 34 — two nonlinear blowups shared one mechanism {#sec-nb-iter34}

Drive-amplitude extrapolation in Euler--Bernoulli and near-eigenvalue
extrapolation in rotational Euler both activated uncontrolled higher-order
interactions. The common mechanism was implicit polynomial degree, not label
noise or a single dataset.

### Iteration 35 — declaring quadratic degree was the constructive fix {#sec-nb-iter35}

A model with exactly one licensed bilinear composition preserved the desired
linear path while representing quadratic response. It reduced the nonlinear
extrapolation failures. The broader design rule is to expose the smallest
known response degree rather than ask an unrestricted nonlinear map to infer
it.

### Iteration 36 — solver-labeled Navier--Stokes exposed the next limit {#sec-nb-iter36}

The first nonlinear solver-labeled suite separated velocity and pressure
behavior across Reynolds number. The nonlinear typed model improved pressure,
but velocity remained difficult and the steady solver itself imposed an
upper-Reynolds validity boundary.

### Iteration 37 — the low-Re band corrected the first explanation {#sec-nb-iter37}

The expected monotone velocity gap with Reynolds number did not appear. A
near-Stokes band and fidelity checks showed that part of the deficit was a
representation issue and part belonged to the finite-resolution steady solve.
This prevented a convection-only story.

### Iteration 38 — parity, capacity, and read-in class were disentangled {#sec-nb-iter38}

A linear model with the same pseudoscalar implementation and closer capacity
isolated the read-in class. The revision held: pressure needed nonlinear
degree, while the residual velocity gap could not be attributed to missing
pseudoscalar channels alone.

## 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-22 — industrial benchmarks, then transfer failure {#sec-nb-industrial-program}

### 2026-07-05 — pivot to AirFRANS and DrivAerML {#sec-nb-industrial-pivot}

The program moved from controlled PDEs to solver-labeled aerodynamic
benchmarks to test whether the learned mechanisms remained realistic
geometry and fields. This was explicitly an external-validity phase, not a
replacement for the controlled mechanism studies.

### AirFRANS protocol v1 — parity typing transferred; declared far-field decay did not {#sec-nb-airfrans-v1}

Across replicated seeds, pseudoscalar typing improved all volume fields and
was especially strong under angle-of-attack extrapolation. A prescribed
far-field decay envelope made the wake task worse. The useful transferable
prior was type symmetry; the inappropriate prior was point-singularity decay
for an extended turbulent wake.

### H4 — learned capacity beat a declared viscous scale {#sec-nb-h4-verdict}

A capacity-matched learned radial pathway decisively outperformed the
declared viscous-scale feature. The declared feature also created an
unfavorable numerical scale. This refuted the belief that naming a plausible
physical length is sufficient; a prior must improve the held-out behavior it
claims to organize.

### Log-radial features improved AirFRANS, with an instability caveat {#sec-nb-v-verdicts}

Learned log-radial features improved the clean-seed median, while one seed
showed a deterministic edge-of-stability event. The feature earned an
AirFRANS role, but its gain was not evidence for a universal physical scale.

### Angle-of-attack extrapolation supported the parity mechanism {#sec-nb-extrapolation}

The parity-typed model transferred especially well to angle-of-attack
extrapolation, where handedness changes are essential. This was
mechanism-consistent external evidence, though still within one dataset
family.

### Trace on AirFRANS — a small, uncertain benefit {#sec-nb-t1-verdict}

Trace information won four of five paired seeds under two conventions, but
the median improvement was only about 20--35% and the registered effect size
had not been specified sharply enough. The result is weak support, not a
confirmation.

### AirFRANS tail — learning rate removed anomalies at an accuracy cost {#sec-nb-tail-verdict}

A lower learning rate removed all registered anomalous seeds but exceeded the
allowed clean-seed cost. The instability was real and seed-dependent; the
operating point remained a trade-off rather than a solved architectural
issue.

### AirFRANS large-batch study — gradient-noise regularization mattered {#sec-nb-b22-verdict}

Matching optimizer-update count at large batch recovered little of the
small-batch advantage. The difference was therefore not just “more steps.”
This is an optimization result that affects fair comparison, not a new
surrogate mechanism.

### Reynolds-band study — difficulty was U-shaped {#sec-nb-e1-curve}

Model error was smallest at intermediate Reynolds number and larger in both
near-Stokes and advective bands. The label-noise floor increased with
Reynolds number but remained orders below model error. A monotone
“higher Reynolds is harder” narrative was refuted.

### Steady-solver scope — practical ceiling near Reynolds 5000 {#sec-nb-re-ceiling-final}

The data generator ceased to converge reliably above roughly Reynolds 5000 at
the tested resolution. Claims beyond that point would mix surrogate error
with an invalid steady-label regime, so the benchmark scope was capped.

### 2026-07-06 — DrivAerML exposed a scale-sensitive drive path {#sec-nb-drivaer-smoke}

Raw freestream magnitude and tunnel-scale coordinates jointly overflowed the
norm-free drive stream. An intrinsic or consistently nondimensional gauge
removed the numerical failure. This justified scale scrutiny, but not the
later claim that a fixed gauge caused cross-family failure.

### H-ground — the global comparison was inconclusive {#sec-nb-hground-verdict}

One-seed vehicle-only, all-boundary, and pooled variants were level.
Subsequent localized-band work never completed under a clean common protocol.
**EDIT:** the correct status is incomplete, not a refutation of boundary
context.

### GeoTransolver gap — rival explanations were registered {#sec-nb-geot-gap}

The large DrivAerML gap was decomposed into field imbalance, optimizer,
boundary supervision, capacity, and propagation hypotheses before further
architecture changes. This was the right scientific pivot: stop climbing
small rungs until the dominant discrepancy is localized.

### GeoTransolver gap — no single field or optimizer explained it {#sec-nb-geot-gap-verdict}

The gap was broad across fields and appeared from the first epochs under the
same trainer. The strongest remaining explanation was architectural credit
assignment on the surface task, with model scale as a later-discovered major
factor.

### Configuration inspection excluded an optimizer explanation {#sec-nb-t3-launch}

GeoTransolver and MeshTransformer used the same training implementation in the
DrivAerML recipe. That eliminated optimizer choice as the explanation for the
large epoch-efficiency difference without another run.

### Trace mode — scientific intervention {#sec-nb-trace-mode}

The trace arm supplied the boundary jump relation at surface queries, where
the previous decoder had an ambiguous self interaction. The relevant
scientific change was access to a boundary-trace channel; implementation
verification is archived separately.

### Trace verdict — real effect, exaggerated prediction {#sec-nb-trace-verdict}

Trace reduced validation error by about twofold and broke the existing
plateau, but failed the registered fivefold bar. It earned a role as a
essential mechanism, not as the complete explanation of the gap.

### Trace factorial — dominant channel, narrower mechanism claim {#sec-nb-trace-factorial-verdict}

At flagship capacity, the registered factorial measured about a 3.8-fold
trace benefit. Its correction and readout components partly substituted for
one another.

**EDIT:** this establishes the marginal value of a trace channel under the
protocol. It does not uniquely identify the earlier “boundary
self-identification” story.

### Capacity ladder — depth helped, rank did not {#sec-nb-t2-verdict}

At fixed protocol, additional boundary-processing depth improved error while
greater attention rank did not. This identified compositional capacity, not a
wider bottleneck, as the useful scaling direction.

### Local-corrector probes — triple null {#sec-nb-probes-verdict}

Three registered local-geometry corrections did not improve efficiency or
final error on the stronger base. Their earlier benefit had been subsumed by
depth and learned members. The correct decision was to stop adding local
correctors.

### Flagship composition — mechanisms stacked in distribution {#sec-nb-flagship-verdict}

Trace, learned members, width, and depth combined to reach a substantially
lower in-family DrivAerML error at three seeds. This established an
in-distribution operating point; it did not establish transfer.

### Kernel factorial — conditional learned-member value, not exact-kernel sufficiency {#sec-nb-factorial-verdict}

The member factorial separated exact and learned dictionary contributions on
the flagship base. Later audit showed the “exact-only” arm still contained a
nonlinear query network and learned projection.

**EDIT:** the factorial measures marginal dictionary value conditional on
that query network. It does not show that exact layer kernels alone carry the
prediction.

### Scale-versus-iteration question {#sec-nb-hc2}

Matched comparisons were registered to distinguish repeated refinement from
plain parameter count. The intentionally boring hypothesis—model scale—was
tested before inventing more elaborate mechanisms.

### Scale-versus-iteration verdict — parameters carried the gain {#sec-nb-hc2-verdict}

Increasing exchange rounds at matched parameter count did not help, while
increasing width sharply improved the floor. The remaining GeoTransolver gap
was therefore much smaller at matched scale, though its early-epoch advantage
remained.

### Scale-law preregistration — measure at the rival's parameter budget {#sec-nb-scalelaw}

The next rung was chosen to match GeoTransolver's parameter count rather than
extrapolate from smaller models. A prediction band and stopping rule were
written before the result.

### Scale-law verdict — predictable improvement, flattening returns {#sec-nb-scalelaw-verdict}

The scale law fit the registered rungs, but its local slope flattened near the
top. Seed variation was large enough that single-rung single-seed differences
could not bear architectural claims.

### GeoTransolver-budget rung — the gap remained {#sec-nb-x2l8-verdict}

At approximately matched parameter count, MeshTransformer fell within its
prediction band but remained about 2.3 times worse. Pure scaling was stopped;
the next gain needed a better mechanism or supervision target.

### Resolution study — more source support helped strongly {#sec-nb-sr-verdict}

Doubling sampled surface support improved the flagship well beyond its
registered bar. This made source resolution a confirmed accuracy axis, but
did not yet distinguish better geometric coverage from a model-specific
sampling optimum.

### Large-batch control — batch size changed the optimization outcome {#sec-nb-mn-verdict}

Larger distributed batches degraded the final error across scale rungs.
Batch size therefore had to be held fixed in scientific comparisons. The
result informs experimental control; it is not an architectural advance.

### DrivAerML OOD protocol — within-family geometry axes {#sec-nb-ood-protocol}

Two held-out geometry directions were constructed from the dataset's design
variables: wake-topology and ride-height extremes. They test extrapolation
within the generative family, not transfer to a new vehicle family.

### Zero-shot within-family OOD — no cliff, but tiny clean sets {#sec-nb-ood-zeroshot}

On the unseen subset left after overlap accounting, degradation was
small. The sample sizes were only ten and four cases, so this was evidence
against an immediate boundary cliff, not a precise transfer estimate.

### GeoTransolver zero-shot comparison — no architecture separation {#sec-nb-geot-ood-zeroshot}

GeoTransolver also showed little degradation on the shallow OOD sets. The
prediction that MeshTransformer's structure would create a clear robustness
advantage was refuted at this depth.

### Corrected vector metric — both models lost wall-shear direction {#sec-nb-corrected-zeroshot}

The original wall-shear aggregate ignored vector direction. Under the
corrected joint-component metric, both architectures showed a similar shallow
OOD penalty and direction error dominated magnitude error.

### Deep within-family OOD — absolute transfer held {#sec-nb-ood-deep-verdict}

Models retrained with full extreme sets held out degraded only a few percent
on their own deep splits. This is strong evidence for interpolation across
the designed DrivAerML family, conditional on retraining and the same data
pipeline.

### Deep OOD differential — modest advantage, not a universal claim {#sec-nb-deep-differential}

On the deeper ride-height split, MeshTransformer degraded less than the
GeoTransolver anchor under the corrected metric. The seed ranges separated,
but the comparison remained within one vehicle family and one benchmark
construction.

### External review — three material corrections {#sec-nb-review}

Review uncovered a direction-blind wall-shear metric, selection/provenance
weaknesses, and an overstrong reading of the exact-kernel factorial. The
metric was corrected and the causal claim was demoted. The durable lesson is
that external-validity evidence needs raw predictions and a fixed metric, not
only training curves.

### Industrial kernel factorial — exact kernels did not explain the flagship {#sec-nb-factorial-verdict-industrial}

At flagship scale, removing learned kernel members caused only a modest
in-family penalty, far below the registered thesis prediction.

**EDIT:** because the remaining query network was still expressive, this
demotes the claim that the exact dictionary is the dominant industrial
mechanism; it does not prove exact singular structure is useless.

### OOD rider — dictionary choice did not change the robustness slope {#sec-nb-rider-verdict}

Exact-only and learned-only dictionary variants degraded similarly on the
within-family OOD splits. Exact members retained a modest absolute-error and
parameter-efficiency benefit, but no measured robustness advantage.

### Five-seed wall-shear result — accepted only as provisional {#sec-nb-seal-verdict}

The recovered raw arrays reproduce a within-family wall-shear differential,
but the historical prose mixed two metric definitions and the experimental
units were not as clean as claimed.

**EDIT:** “sealed” is withdrawn. The result is provisional and does not carry
the cross-family argument.

### Cross-family transfer — preregistered decisive test {#sec-nb-crossfamily-prereg}

Existing DrivAerML checkpoints were frozen before evaluation on an untouched
SHIFT-SUV family. No tuning, case exclusion, or post-hoc metric choice was
allowed. This was the first test aligned with the program's strongest
generalization claim.

### Cross-family verdict — the model failed decisively {#sec-nb-crossfam-verdict}

Every tested MeshTransformer checkpoint produced nonphysical zero-shot
outputs on the untouched SHIFT-SUV set, while GeoTransolver degraded but
remained structured. This falsified the released model's cross-family claim.

**EDIT:** after this first read, the same SHIFT cases became a development
set. Later gauge scans and architecture variants are hypothesis-generating,
not independent confirmations. The failure was real; its initially proposed
fixed-gauge cause was not.

### Program check-in — synthetic mechanisms strong, industrial claim weak {#sec-nb-checkin-2}

The controlled program had isolated useful representation rules. The
industrial program had achieved strong in-family accuracy but not the stated
cross-family objective. Subsequent work therefore had to repair the
measurement and transfer hypotheses rather than widen the flagship.

## 2026-07-22 to 2026-07-27 — transfer hypotheses and evidence audit {#sec-nb-transfer-repair}

### Intrinsic gauge calibration — protocol violation {#sec-nb-gauge-calib}

The proposed intrinsic scale constant was labeled train-only, but the
calibration iterator included held-out DrivAerML cases. The sampled RMS
statistic also inherited unmeasured sampling bias.

**EDIT:** the numerical constant cannot support a train-only transfer claim.
The algebraic covariance argument for an intrinsic gauge remains; this
calibration does not.

### Gauge acceptance — not a drop-in transformation {#sec-nb-gauge-accept-verdict}

The intrinsic transform was inert for GeoTransolver, as expected, but changed
existing MeshTransformer predictions beyond the registered preservation
threshold. It therefore required retraining and could not be used as a
post-hoc repair.

### Transfer-v2 preregistration — retrain before looking {#sec-nb-transfer-v2-prereg}

The second transfer attempt froze training, evaluation, and acceptance rules
before any intrinsic-trained checkpoint or SHIFT-SUV result existed. Its
purpose was to test the fixed-gauge causal story, not merely produce a better
number.

### Measure-matching gauge test — the causal prediction failed {#sec-nb-measmech-verdict}

Matching the total empirical measure by changing the gauge did not restore
the training-resolution prediction. Because the gauge also changed geometry,
the intervention was confounded, but the specific causal prediction was
refuted.

### Random-initialization normalization probe — mechanism story weakened {#sec-nb-measnorm-caveat}

Normalization barely changed resolution behavior at random initialization,
and the unnormalized operator did not scale with source count as predicted.
The catastrophic resolution dependence therefore lived mainly in learned
weights, not a simple unnormalized sum.

### Coverage augmentation — registered but not accepted as an architecture result {#sec-nb-hca-launch}

Training over several source counts tested whether the model had learned a
coverage-specific compensation. This was a data-support intervention, not a
new surrogate mechanism, and its interpretation remained entangled with how
the surface was sampled.

### Singularity subtraction — mechanism replicated, magnitude corrected {#sec-nb-subtraction-replication}

An independent reconstruction confirmed that subtracting the singular local
term can reduce variance in subsampled boundary integration. The originally
reported gains were overstated by roughly four to ten times. The remaining
result supports singularity-aware quadrature, not the claim that it alone
explains industrial transfer.

### 2026-07-27 — stop widening; repair the empirical measure {#sec-program-review}

The controlled synthetic program remained scientifically productive, but the
industrial transfer claim did not. The current model failed on untouched
SHIFT-SUV geometry, and the training-resolution optimum confounded source
coverage, query coverage, and scoring measure.

**Decision.** Freeze new industrial architecture arms. Treat the industrial
branch as a measurement-design problem until those three supports can be
varied independently. Return the main research loop to controlled experiments
that distinguish surrogate mechanisms.

## 2026-07-29 — controlled reset and partially known operators {#sec-nb-controlled-reset}

### Canonical replay closes validity, not architecture {#sec-nb-canonical-replay-edit}

On a fixed 36-car cohort, canonical and historical geometry paths were
noninferior with mixed-sign changes below 0.14%. They are algebraically
identical:

$$
\frac{(x-c_v)/L-(c_A-c_v)/L}{8}
=\frac{x-c_A}{8L}.
$$

The remaining difference is floating-point construction order.

**EDIT:** two attempted parity runs produced no scientific result because
they failed before evaluating either arm. Complete byte verification also
covered only four executed cases, not the whole cohort. The accepted
conclusion is validity noninferiority, not an accuracy or architecture gain.

### Scientific status after the reset {#sec-nb-2026-07-29-agenda-reset}

Four controlled results changed the agenda:

| Question | Evidence | Conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Do learned query corrections help Laplace? | Removing them changed held-out error only modestly while reducing normalized Laplacian residual from 0.865 to $1.2\times10^{-13}$. | They have not earned a role on this family; exact propagation is simpler and more faithful. |
| Is remaining error density inference or boundary resolution? | Solving the density mattered little on coarse boundaries but about fifteenfold at the finest tested resolution. | They are sequential bottlenecks. |
| Was historical low-screening collapse physical? | A correctly normalized double layer stayed stable as screening vanished. | No; the old mechanism claim came from an invalid instrument. |
| Does one known-operator solver transfer? | A shared residual-controlled double layer converged on all 160 parameter/geometry cases and improved monotonically under refinement. | Parameter- or geometry-conditioned iteration was unnecessary in this controlled setting. |

The current architectural hypothesis became: encode licensed singular
structure, infer boundary density through a trace-residual process, and learn
only the smooth part not fixed by the known operator.

**EDIT:** an earlier version also claimed that freely learned singular
coefficients had failed. The registered experiment below shows that statement
was premature.

### Singular form transfers; hard fixation does not {#sec-nb-principal-part-result}

[]{#sec-nb-principal-part-transfer}
**Question.** The leading double-layer singularity is universal across the
controlled drift--screening family. Must its amplitude therefore be fixed
analytically, or is it enough to constrain the form and learn one global
amplitude?

**Evidence.** Preserving the singular order and angular structure reduced
interpolation and near-boundary error by roughly fifteenfold relative to an
unstructured kernel. The learned amplitude settled within 0.4% of the
analytic coefficient. Hard fixation, however, improved near-boundary error by
only 5% and fine-resolution error by 26%, and did not improve parameter
transfer consistently. Every representation still struggled at strong
screening.

**Belief update.** The singular *form* is transferable; exact fixation of its
coefficient has not earned the loss of flexibility. Retain a tightly
constrained amplitude and direct learning toward the smooth remainder.

### Solution-aligned supervision improves interpolation, not operator transfer {#sec-nb-supervision-alignment-result}

[]{#sec-nb-supervision-alignment}
**Question.** Is extrapolation failing because pointwise kernel fitting
weights the wrong object, rather than because the representation is wrong?
The falsifier required downstream supervision to improve held-out operator
parameters without sacrificing unseen boundary functions or refinement.

**Evidence.** A hybrid kernel-and-solution objective reduced interpolation,
unseen-boundary, and unseen-geometry errors by 65%, 66%, and 74% relative to
pointwise kernel fitting. It did not pass the field-and-trace transfer test at
any operator extreme. Solution-only training was especially revealing: its
field predictions were accurate in band while its boundary-trace residual was
about thirteen times larger. The composed solution can therefore be right
while its purported operator factors are wrong.

**Belief update.** Hybrid supervision is the best in-band objective here, but
loss alignment is not the missing transfer mechanism. Stop varying the loss;
retain independent operator-fidelity diagnostics.

### Sufficient similarity variables are not a sufficient representation {#sec-nb-similarity-coordinates-result}

[]{#sec-nb-similarity-coordinates}
**Question.** Would the physically sufficient dimensionless drift and
screening coordinates turn parameter extrapolation into interpolation?

**Evidence.** They improved the strong-screening field by about 24% and its
trace residual by 39%--70%. The same change made interpolation 2.2--2.9 times
worse, more than tripled fine-resolution error, and harmed the low-screening
limit and stronger-drift case. No joint transfer criterion passed.

**Belief update.** Coordinate sufficiency is not approximation sufficiency
across competing asymptotic regimes. Keep the useful variables, but encode
the limiting response in the output factorization instead of replacing the
raw coordinates.

### Program check-in — operator extrapolation remains the bottleneck {#sec-nb-asymptotic-checkin}

At this point, explicit singular structure, a boundary trace solve, and
hybrid supervision had produced strong interpolation, unseen-geometry, and
unseen-boundary performance. Hard coefficient fixation, solution-aligned
losses, and similarity coordinates had all failed the same operator-transfer
test. The next useful question was therefore whether one learned transition
could be scaffolded by the two known asymptotic limits, not whether another
generic feature or loss would help.

### A two-limit carrier makes the operator transition learnable {#sec-nb-asymptotic-carrier-result}

[]{#sec-nb-asymptotic-carrier}
**Hypothesis.** Strong screening forces an unconstrained remainder to cancel
the singular term before producing a decaying kernel. A carrier that is exact
in the weak- and strong-screening limits should leave only a smooth bounded
transition to learn. The critical control was the fixed carrier: if it
matched the learned model, learning had not earned its role.

**Evidence.** The fixed carrier improved both screening extremes but made
interpolation roughly four times worse. Adding a bounded learned transition
reduced field error relative to the raw learned kernel by factors of 8.7 in
band, 14.8 at weak screening, 31.6 at strong screening, and 33.6 under
stronger drift. It also beat the fixed carrier decisively, so the learned
transition was necessary.

**Belief update.** The useful factorization is: carry the singular and
asymptotic limits exactly, then learn only the smooth transition. This
substantially strengthens the constant-coefficient result, but it does not
show transfer to a different local operator.

**Decision.** Stop modifying coordinates and losses on this family. Introduce
spatially varying coefficients, where local asymptotics remain valid but no
single global Green response is supplied.

### Ordered coefficient information is necessary but pooling cannot compose it {#sec-nb-variable-coefficient-context-result}

[]{#sec-nb-variable-coefficient-context}
**Question.** Two layered coefficient profiles can share every scalar optical
summary yet differ only in layer order. Because their local propagators do
not commute, they have different boundary-to-interior operators. Can a
position-aware pooled encoder recover that distinction?

**Evidence.** Scalar-summary models recovered none of the intentionally
matched order contrast, as required by the information argument. Giving a
pooled model ordered samples reduced field error but recovered only 8%--52%
of the true contrast, far below the registered 80% bar. A
constant-coefficient carrier remained a useful specialist but did not repair
the missing composition.

**Belief update.** Ordered information is necessary, but merely presenting it
to a feed-forward pool is insufficient. The computation itself must respect
physical order.

### Physical-order composition recovers noncommuting layered response {#sec-nb-path-ordered-generator-result}

[]{#sec-nb-path-ordered-generator}
**Hypothesis.** Local operator variation should be represented by local model
updates composed in physical order. Sorting those same updates supplied the
decisive negative control.

**Evidence.** Physical-order composition recovered 97.9%--99.2% of the
matched layer-order contrast and reduced paired error twenty-sixfold relative
to pooled ordered samples. Sorting the same local maps erased the contrast
exactly. The model nevertheless did not improve the strong-coefficient case
consistently; correct composition did not automatically identify an
extrapolative local law.

**Belief update.** Noncommuting operator variation should be represented by
noncommuting model updates. Composition and constitutive extrapolation are
separate problems.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** a proposed follow-up would have asked the model to
relearn the already-known local reaction law. That would test an
unknown-closure problem, not this PDE. The stronger next test supplies the
known local operator and asks whether ordered composition remains local mode
coupling.

### Program check-in — ordered composition is supported, physical breadth is not {#sec-nb-ordered-program-checkin}

The constant-coefficient carrier and layered composition results were now
strong. The open scientific debt was breadth: all heterogeneous tests still
separated into independent transverse modes on a fixed interval. The next
experiment therefore changed the physics by coupling modes, without adding a
new exact global solution formula. The strategic risk was clear: a mechanism
that worked only in separable reductions would be a bespoke reduced solver,
not a general surrogate principle.

### Physical-order composition remains coupled modes and longer paths {#sec-nb-coupled-path-order-result}

[]{#sec-nb-coupled-path-order}
**Question.** Does the ordered-composition result hold when local
eigendirections rotate, so independent scalar channels are mathematically
impossible?

**Evidence.** The physical-order model recovered 98.3%--99.5% of the
permutation contrast. Relative to position-aware pooling, it reduced paired
field error by a factor of 17.7, unseen-twist cross-channel error by 44, and
doubled-path cross-channel error by 38. Sorting erased the contrast. A global
metric would have hidden the failure: pooling had about 1% total error but
24%--25% error in the coupling blocks.

**Belief update.** Ordered composition is a reusable principle across scalar
and coupled layered systems. Cross-channel fidelity must remain a primary
metric because the uncoupled response dominates aggregate norms.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** “longer paths” meant only the tested doubled path. This
experiment established order sensitivity at that finite depth; it did not show
that approximation error remains bounded as composition depth grows.

**Decision.** Move to a nonseparable coefficient field and ask whether the
heterogeneous correction admits a compact *transferable* state, not merely a
compact after-the-fact factorization.

### Rank four is an oracle ceiling, not yet a dynamics {#sec-nb-nonseparable-rank-result}

[]{#sec-nb-nonseparable-rank}
**Question.** Is the cross-channel correction in the first nonseparable field
small enough to justify a low-rank surrogate?

**Evidence.** The best per-case rank-four factorization left about 12%
cross-channel error; rank three left about 24%, and fixed or global rank-four
subspaces remained near 31%. Yet the entire coupled correction contributed
only 0.12%--0.52% of the full operator norm. Aggregate accuracy would call the
uncoupled model solved while missing the phenomenon under study.

**Belief update.** Rank four was sufficient to justify one learned test, but
only as an oracle ceiling. Its factors were selected after seeing each
solution and did not imply a realizable shared dynamics.

### Ordered rank-four recurrence works in band but not across spectra {#sec-nb-nonseparable-latent-result}

[]{#sec-nb-nonseparable-latent}
**Hypothesis.** A rank-four state updated in physical order should approach
the per-case ceiling better than a global compression and transfer to unseen
coefficient variation.

**Evidence.** Physical order reduced global rank-four error by 31% in band and
36% at strong heterogeneity. The breadth claim failed on every replicate:
fast-variation error exceeded fixed truncation by more than twofold, and
sorting was actually better on the fast fields. The recurrence had learned
how smooth training sequences usually unfold, not a local law.

**Belief update.** Ordering remains useful, but generic recurrence is not the
transferable mechanism. A valid local update needs a continuum limit tied to
physical path length.

### A continuum latent flow fixes discretization, not frequency breadth {#sec-nb-nonseparable-flow-result}

[]{#sec-nb-nonseparable-flow}
**Question.** Was the recurrence failing because every layer counted as one
abstract update, regardless of its physical width?

**Evidence.** Scaling the update by path length made the learned flow stable
from four to thirty-two layers; its finest-grid error stayed within 3% of its
training-grid error, whereas the old recurrence deteriorated roughly
sixfold. On faster coefficient fields, however, it remained 1.7--2.1 times
worse than fixed truncation and did not consistently beat the sorted control.

**Belief update.** Continuum consistency is real and necessary. It removes a
discretization bug in the hypothesis, but it does not produce a
frequency-independent low-rank law.

### Broader spectral support reallocates error; it does not reveal one local law {#sec-nb-frequency-coverage-result}

[]{#sec-nb-frequency-coverage}
**Question.** Is the remaining failure merely missing training coverage?

**Evidence.** Broader training reduced error on newly covered fast fields by
26%--33%, but increased smooth-field error by 30%--74%. It remained 33% worse
than fixed truncation even on covered frequencies and 36%--66% worse on
unseen frequencies.

**Belief update.** At fixed state size, the flow reallocates accuracy toward
the spectra it sees rather than learning one transferable propagation law.
The learned rank-four flow branch is closed.

### A connection-correct moving subspace provides no accuracy {#sec-nb-adaptive-subspace-result}

[]{#sec-nb-adaptive-subspace}
**Question.** Could a physics-derived moving rank-four eigenspace realize the
static oracle without learning a new flow?

**Evidence.** Ignoring basis rotation was catastrophic. Applying the exact
connection reduced shifted-spectrum errors by factors of 2.0--2.6, confirming
that the connection is essential coordinate bookkeeping. Once corrected,
the moving subspace matched fixed and global truncation to within about 1%
and was slightly worse on every aggregate split.

**Belief update.** The static rank-four oracle is not evidence for a useful
low-rank propagation mechanism. End this branch. Future composition should
retain a richer hidden physical state and compress only at readout when justified.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the last sentence was too binary. The moving-basis
model supplied coordinate bookkeeping but no closure for modes discarded by
projection. Some learned arms instead carried a higher-dimensional recurrent
summary while constraining only the correction rank. The experiments therefore
did not isolate full physical state from compressed state with
projection-induced memory. They refute the tested constructions, not
low-dimensional state in principle.

### Program check-in — stop optimizing the toy compression {#sec-nb-low-rank-checkin}

Three principles remain after the controlled program:

1. carry exact boundary, singular, and limiting structure rather than
   relearning it;
2. compose spatially varying local operators in physical order; and
3. scale learned local updates with physical path length.

The rank-four program also produced a clean refutation. An after-the-fact
low-rank correction exists, but recurrence, continuum flow, broader training,
and a connection-correct moving eigenspace all fail to make it a transferable
computation.

| Research claim | Current confidence | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Reusable constant-coefficient boundary mechanism | 90% | Strong within the controlled families; untested on a different operator. |
| Reusable physical-order mechanism for layered coefficients | 90% | Supported for scalar and coupled modes. |
| Transferable rank-four dynamics for nonseparable coefficients | 15% | Refuted for the tested natural constructions. |
| General variable-coefficient surrogate with a richer hidden state | 45% | Open; the state and geometry interaction are not identified. |
| Defensible industrial cross-family gain | 25% | Unearned after the untouched family-shift failure. |

**Research decision.** Stop optimizing the rank-four toy. The next decisive
question is whether the remaining principles help on a geometry-bearing
problem when discarded physical state is either retained or given a valid
closure. That question is not yet preregistered or launched.

## 2026-07-29 — Research questions replace component specifications {#sec-nb-agenda-altitude-reset}

The program had begun to turn possible explanations into a detailed
architecture before the evidence could choose among them. That was the wrong
altitude for the notebook.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the preceding theory correctly names several ways a
surrogate might fail, but it does not establish that the eventual model needs
a particular port, latent rank, carrier, recurrence, or composition law. Any
earlier wording that presented those candidates as requirements is withdrawn.
They remain hypotheses only.

Four findings remain after this correction:

1. Boundary-aware structure can improve accuracy, fidelity, or efficiency on
   controlled PDE families.
2. More structure is not automatically better; several plausible additions
   were neutral or harmful, and some historical comparisons were invalid.
3. A compact representation that works on one controlled family has not yet
   shown that it retains enough information when geometry and operators change.
4. The current industrial model does not transfer to an untouched vehicle
   family.

The research program is therefore organized around three rival explanations:

| Rival explanation | Observation that would count against it |
|---|---|
| A task-adaptive physical representation is necessary for broad transfer. | A matched generic operator transfers and scales equally well without the proposed structure. |
| A sufficiently capable generic operator can discover the needed representation. | Its failures repeatedly follow a missing physical information channel that a matched structured model repairs. |
| Boundary-driven PDE families are too different for one useful architecture. | The same high-level design rule produces a repeatable advantage across different propagation classes. |

The next scientific decision is not which component to implement. First,
finish the validity audit and retain only conclusions that remain valid after confirmed
bugs and protocol corrections. Then define one benchmark capable of separating
the three explanations above with frozen models, untouched shifts, and a
steel-manned generic baseline. More toy latent variants, loss sweeps, and
isolated architectural features are explicitly out of scope until that
benchmark exists.

No computation was launched for this agenda correction.

## Exploratory theory notes retained for provenance

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Background reasoning, not the active agenda"}
These notes preserve the reasoning that led to the agenda correction. They are
candidate mechanisms and failure modes, not an implementation plan or a list
of settled architectural requirements.

### Agenda correction — geometry is a state-identification problem {#sec-nb-geometry-state-agenda}

**Question.** When the shape changes, what information must a surrogate retain
so that boundary forcing still reaches the correct interior response?

A change of coordinates from a physical domain to a fixed reference domain
turns geometry into a spatially varying tensor coefficient. Geometry is
therefore part of the operator, not static metadata. It can mix physical
channels as the solution propagates, which links geometry transfer to the
earlier evidence for physical-order composition.

Two existing benchmarks cannot answer the question. Conformal
two-dimensional Laplace problems can make reference transport exact, while
the controlled screened problem already transferred across its tested
deformations. Repeating either would measure an easy invariance rather than
identify what a general surrogate must remember.

Four explanations remain live:

1. **State sufficiency:** a compact state discards channels that later geometry
   can make observable.
2. **Closure:** a compact present state can work, but only if it represents the
   nonlocal influence of discarded channels.
3. **Persistent geometry:** the state is adequate, but local geometry must
   remain available throughout propagation rather than only at the input.
4. **Reference locality:** any one-reference residual becomes unreliable once
   the new shape is too far from its reference.

The first scientific gate is therefore not a model comparison. It is an
information-flow measurement: determine how quickly boundary influence
compresses within each geometry, whether the leading transferable subspaces
align across geometries, and whether an omitted channel can
become observable again downstream. Those measurements would distinguish
state size, closure, and geometry-retention explanations before an
architecture is chosen.

[]{#sec-nb-projection-memory-length}
**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the earlier proposal specified model arms and numerical
acceptance thresholds before this information question had been answered.
Those details were implementation-led and have been withdrawn from the
research ledger. A second overstatement called omitted-mode influence
“memory.” In an elliptic boundary-value problem the precise possibility is a
bilateral spatial closure, not causal temporal memory. Raw nonadditivity
between two geometric perturbations also cannot isolate discarded channels,
because retained channels rescatter too; a retained-state control is required.

**Decision.** Hold geometry-model development. First establish which of the
four information mechanisms is present.

### Transfer spectra bound only the compressible part {#sec-nb-transfer-spectrum-state}

For a coercive elliptic problem, a transfer operator maps arbitrary boundary
data on an outer interface to the solution on a separated inner interface.
[Smetana and Patera](https://ris.utwente.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/168414349/15m1009603.pdf)
show that its leading left singular vectors give the best fixed-dimensional
linear port space; the first omitted singular value is the worst-case
transfer error. [Babuška and Lipton](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~lipton/OptimalBasis.pdf)
show rapid asymptotic local approximation for uniformly elliptic problems
even with rough coefficients, although that result does not guarantee a
small dimension at finite separation or extreme contrast.

This gives a scientific criterion for elliptic compression: state size should
be earned by decay of the transfer spectrum, not selected as an architectural
hyperparameter. Across changing geometry, three outcomes are possible:

- rapid decay and aligned leading spaces support one fixed compact state;
- rapid decay but rotating leading spaces support a geometry-conditioned
  state; and
- slow decay rejects compact local state in the tested regime.

Existing geometry evidence does not decide among them. In
[Smetana's cracked-beam study](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02946), a port space
could be reused accurately at moderate tolerance, while a tighter target
required a larger joint space than either geometry alone. That supports
measuring both spectral decay and cross-geometry alignment.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the earlier rank-four study measured a completed
correction matrix after each solution was known. It did not measure the
Kolmogorov width of the local solution family or the state needed for
arbitrary boundary data. It therefore refutes the tested rank-four dynamics,
not compact state in principle.

**Decision.** For coercive elliptic systems, transfer decay and subspace
alignment are prerequisites for any state-compression claim. This criterion
does not yet extend to every PDE class.

### Propagation class decides what may be compressed {#sec-nb-propagation-class}

The emerging agenda cannot be based on elliptic smoothing alone. Canonical
equations separate boundary information into qualitatively different classes:

| Propagation class | What happens to boundary information | Research implication |
|---|---|---|
| Coercive elliptic or diffusive | Fine-scale channels decay across physical separation. | Spectrum-certified compression is plausible after enough separation. |
| Wave or Helmholtz | Propagating channels do not decay; only evanescent channels do. Near cutoff, decay can become arbitrarily slow. | Preserve every propagating channel; the irreducible state grows with frequency and cross-section. |
| Pure transport | The downstream trace is a translated upstream trace, with no smoothing. | Arbitrary boundary functions require a distributed state unless the admissible input class is restricted. |

The wave statement follows directly by separating a waveguide into transverse
modes: modes below cutoff propagate, while modes above cutoff decay. The
transport statement is even sharper. For $u_t+c\,u_x=0$, the solution
$u(t,x)=g(x-ct)$ is a norm-preserving translation of the input. Translation on
an unrestricted infinite-dimensional boundary space is not compact, so no
fixed finite-dimensional linear state can have a uniformly small worst-case
error.

This distinction agrees with primary approximation results. For linear
transport, [Arbes, Greif, and Urban](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00066) show
that the Kolmogorov-width rate depends on the boundary data: a jump can give
slow $N^{-1/2}$ decay, while smoother or analytic data can be much more
compressible. For the linear heat equation,
[Schleuß and Smetana](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.02759) prove compactness of a
local space-time transfer operator under their stated diffusion assumptions;
their exponential singular-value decay is numerical evidence, not a universal
rate theorem.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** “transfer spectra should set state dimension” was too
broad if read as a universal rule. The corrected rule is: first identify and
preserve nondecaying channels; then use transfer-spectrum decay to size only
the evanescent or smoothing remainder. If the relevant transfer is
noncompact, increasing a fixed latent rank is not a principled cure. Any
observed compactness may instead come from restrictions in the data
distribution.

**Program hypothesis.** A general boundary-driven surrogate should preserve
the boundary contract and nondecaying physical channels, compress only
spectrum-certified residual channels, and learn geometry-induced conversion
between them in physical order. The amount and type of state should therefore
vary with propagation class rather than be universal.

A decisive future test would examine the predicted qualitative scaling across
matched canonical problems: elliptic state should shrink with separation;
wave state should grow with the number of propagating channels and become
difficult near cutoff; and transport state should grow with admissible
boundary bandwidth unless the data class is explicitly restricted. A fixed
latent that transfers without following those scalings would refute this
hypothesis—or reveal that the benchmark never exercised arbitrary boundary
information.

**Decision.** No architecture or compute is launched during the research
pause. The next deliverable is a propagation-class map of what information
must be carried, what may be compressed, and which assumption makes each
claim valid.

### The task contract, not the PDE label, sets compressibility {#sec-nb-information-contract}

**Scientific correction.** Propagation class identifies a mechanism for
preserving or erasing information, but it does not determine a unique state
dimension. The relevant object is the complete task: which boundary functions
are admissible, which operators and geometries vary, how far information must
travel, what must be observed, and at what error tolerance.

In symbols, let $S_\theta$ map boundary data $g$ to a solution for operator and
geometry $\theta$, and let $O_\theta$ extract the requested field, trace, or
quantity of interest. The response family is

$$
\mathcal M(\Theta,\mathcal G,\mathcal O)
=
\{\,O_\theta S_\theta g:
\theta\in\Theta,\ g\in\mathcal G\,\}.
$$

Any statement that this family is “low-dimensional” is incomplete unless
$\Theta$, the boundary class $\mathcal G$, the observation contract
$\mathcal O$, the norm, the tolerance, and the permitted representation class
are fixed.

The primary literature makes this dependence concrete.
[Arbes, Greif, and Urban](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00066) show for linear
transport that a jump can yield $N^{-1/2}$ linear-width decay while analytic
data can yield exponential decay. [Greif and Urban](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.08488)
prove the lower bound $d_N\geq 1/(4\sqrt N)$ for one wave solution family with
discontinuous initial data; it is not a lower bound for every wave problem.
These initial-value results are warnings about the quantifiers, not direct
proofs for this program's boundary-to-interior setting.

Representation class is a separate axis. A translated template may have slow
linear-width decay even though one shift coordinate plus the template
specifies it exactly. Thus a slow Kolmogorov width rejects a small fixed
linear carrier, not every compact nonlinear representation.
[Nonino and colleagues](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.06598) provide empirical
evidence that problem-specific transport maps can accelerate proper
orthogonal decomposition, but their study addresses the offline stage and
does not establish a general online surrogate.

Four rival explanations must therefore be kept separate:

1. **Physical attenuation:** complexity falls with propagation distance even
   when boundary richness is held fixed.
2. **Input restriction:** apparent compactness disappears when the admissible
   boundary family is broadened.
3. **Observation restriction:** a quantity of interest is compact even though
   the full field or boundary trace is not.
4. **Nonlinear alignment:** fixed linear spaces fail, but a physically
   meaningful coordinate transformation exposes a compact residual.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** the preceding propagation-class entry was still too
deterministic if read as “the PDE type sets the latent size.” The corrected
claim is weaker and testable: propagation class predicts how information can
be lost; the declared task contract and representation class determine how
much information the surrogate must retain.

**Research exam, held in reserve.** Before another architecture comparison,
declare the boundary family, operator/geometry family, propagation horizon,
observation norm, tolerance, and approximation class. Then vary boundary
richness, propagation distance, and observation scope independently. Compare
fixed-linear and physically aligned descriptions separately. This distinguishes
physical compression from a narrow dataset, a forgiving observable, or a
coordinate choice.

**Decision.** The next scientific artifact is a compressibility atlas over
these contract axes, not another model. No experiment or compute is launched
during the research pause.

### Canonical limits predict three different compression laws {#sec-nb-compressibility-atlas}

**Derived atlas.** A future surrogate should first be compared with the
information loss already implied by the PDE. Define $r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{lin}}$
as the number of channels a fixed linear carrier must preserve to approximate
a specified boundary-to-observable map within operator-norm error $\epsilon$.
This is a property of the declared task, not the dimension of a neural latent.

The table gives asymptotic scalings for canonical constant-coefficient
problems. Here $L$ is propagation distance, $H$ is strip width, $\nu$ is
diffusivity, $t$ is elapsed diffusion time, $d$ is spatial dimension, $k$ is
Helmholtz wavenumber, and $K$ is a one-dimensional boundary bandwidth.
Boundary conditions and persistent zero modes change constants, not the
qualitative laws.

| Declared map | Physical information law | Predicted fixed-linear complexity |
|---|---|---|
| Elliptic strip boundary $\rightarrow$ interior port separated by $L$ | Transverse modes decay exponentially with mode number and distance. | $r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{lin}}\sim (H/L)\log(1/\epsilon)$. Screening lowers the count further. |
| Heat initial state $\rightarrow$ field after time $t>0$ | Laplacian mode $n$ decays as $\exp(-\nu\lambda_n t)$. | Weyl scaling gives $r_\epsilon^{\mathrm{lin}}\sim [\log(1/\epsilon)/(\nu t)]^{d/2}$, up to domain volume and boundary-condition constants. |
| Helmholtz waveguide port $\rightarrow$ separated port | Roughly $kH/\pi$ transverse channels propagate without decay; higher channels are evanescent. | A floor proportional to $kH/\pi$, plus a tolerance-dependent evanescent tail that worsens near cutoff. |
| Pure transport trace $\rightarrow$ downstream trace | Translation preserves every admitted Fourier mode. | For arbitrary data of bandwidth $K$, complexity grows with $K$ and does not fall with $L$. |

The elliptic scaling follows from the closed-form transfer spectrum in
[Smetana and Patera](https://ris.utwente.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/168414349/15m1009603.pdf).
The heat scaling is derived here from the heat semigroup and Weyl eigenvalue
counting; it concerns observation after positive time, not the full history
including $t=0$. The wave and transport rows follow from transverse-mode and
characteristic decompositions. They are baseline scalings, not universal
theorems for variable coefficients, nonlinear equations, resonant cavities,
or unrestricted geometry families.

The atlas predicts three qualitatively distinct signatures:

1. **Smoothing collapse:** elliptic and diffusive complexity falls with
   separation or elapsed time at fixed input richness.
2. **Propagating floor:** wave complexity cannot fall below the number of
   nondecaying channels and grows with frequency or cross-section.
3. **Data-limited plateau:** transport complexity follows admitted boundary
   bandwidth rather than propagation distance.

A fourth signature distinguishes representation classes. A family of one
translated template can be compact after nonlinear alignment even when its
fixed-linear width decays slowly; arbitrary superpositions of boundary modes
cannot be dismissed by that example.

**Scientific falsifiers, held in reserve.** Failure of elliptic or heat
complexity to decrease under added separation or time would contradict the
smoothing account. A fixed-linear Helmholtz carrier apparently smaller than
the propagating-channel count would indicate that the boundary family omitted
independent channel combinations. Transport complexity falling with distance
would reveal numerical diffusion or a restricted observation. A
single-coordinate alignment helping equally on arbitrary independent
multimode inputs would contradict the claim that it specifically exploits
coherent motion.

**Decision.** Use these scaling shapes as the baseline exams for future
benchmarks. They identify what a surrogate must explain before accuracy
comparisons can support a general architectural claim. No run is launched
during the research pause.

### Universal approximation is eligibility, not generalization {#sec-nb-universality-contract}

**Question.** Do neural-operator universality theorems make the
compressibility atlas irrelevant? No. They ask whether some sufficiently large
model can approximate one declared operator on one declared input set. This
program asks the quantitative question they leave open: how much information,
model capacity, and data are required as the boundary, operator, and geometry
contract broadens?

The theorem quantifiers are decisive:

- [Kovachki, Lanthaler, and Mishra, Theorem 5](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume22/21-0806/21-0806.pdf)
  proves uniform Fourier neural operator approximation for a continuous
  operator on a **compact** subset of a Sobolev space. The approximating model
  may depend on the operator, compact set, and tolerance. Compactness is what
  makes one finite Fourier truncation work uniformly in their proof.
- [Kovachki and colleagues, Theorems 11--13](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume24/21-1524/21-1524.pdf)
  prove the analogous neural-operator result on compact input sets, and a
  separate mean-square result under a fixed probability measure. The latter is
  distributional accuracy, not worst-case accuracy over arbitrary boundary
  data. Their discretization invariance means convergence to a fixed continuum
  model under mesh refinement; it does not enlarge the functions or operator
  families on which that model is accurate.
- [Lu and colleagues, Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.03193) gives
  DeepONet finitely many fixed input sensors only after restricting the inputs
  to a compact subset of continuous functions. For the unrestricted unit ball
  of continuous boundary functions, any finite sensor set misses a continuous
  bump between sensors, so it cannot uniformly identify even the identity map.

**Derived interpretation.** In an infinite-dimensional normed space, a closed
unit ball is not compact in its own norm. A set bounded in a stronger
regularity norm can be compact in a weaker topology, but that is precisely an
input-regularity restriction. An operator or geometry parameter may also be
included as an input, but the theorem must then be applied to a compact joint
family; it gives no claim beyond that family.

Existence also does not imply efficiency. The Fourier neural operator paper
explicitly warns that universality alone is not evidence of computational
viability and gives general cases with exponentially growing model size.
These theorems likewise do not establish sample efficiency, successful
optimization, or transfer to boundary spectra, frequencies, geometries, or
operators absent from the declared set.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** “universal approximation” must not be used in this
program as evidence that a fixed architecture covers arbitrary boundary
functions or family shifts. It establishes only that the model class has no
absolute representational obstruction on each declared compact task. The
compressibility atlas addresses the missing question: how required information
should scale when that task is expanded.

Three rival program hypotheses now remain:

1. **Generic efficiency:** once the contract is fixed, a generic universal
   neural operator follows the task's intrinsic complexity closely; explicit
   physics changes only constants.
2. **Physics efficiency:** generic and structured models may both be
   universal, but a physical carrier materially improves capacity, data, or
   transfer scaling as the contract expands.
3. **Distributional sufficiency:** practical boundary data occupy a narrow
   distribution, making worst-case breadth unnecessary. Success would then
   support a distribution-specific surrogate, not a general boundary-driven
   one.

**Research exam, held in reserve.** Broaden one contract axis at a time:
boundary bandwidth or regularity, propagation frequency or horizon, and
operator or geometry family. At fixed error tolerance, ask how required
capacity and data change, and whether accuracy remains a held-out extension
of that axis. A general architecture supports its claim only if its scaling tracks
the task's information law; interpolation on one compact set establishes
eligibility, not generalization.

**Decision.** Universality is a gate, not evidence for an architecture. The
next agenda question is comparative efficiency under controlled contract
expansion. No experiment or compute is launched during the research pause.

### Generalization has three independent bottlenecks {#sec-nb-three-bottlenecks}

**Agenda result.** A surrogate's total error cannot reveal whether it lost
necessary boundary information, chose an inadequate state carrier, or failed
to learn an otherwise sufficient finite map. Those are different scientific
failures and require different remedies.

Let $T_\theta=O_\theta S_\theta$ denote the declared boundary-to-observable map
for operator and geometry $\theta$. For a geometry-independent boundary
encoder $E$, define the task-aware separation

$$
d_\Theta(g,h)
=
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
\|T_\theta g-T_\theta h\|_{\mathcal Y}.
$$

For any surrogate whose only boundary dependence is through $E$, the equality
$E(g)=E(h)$ gives every downstream predictor the same encoded input for both
boundary functions. The triangle inequality then gives the unavoidable
collision bound

$$
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\max_{v\in\{g,h\}}
\|T_\theta v-\widehat T_\theta v\|_{\mathcal Y}
\geq \tfrac12 d_\Theta(g,h).
$$

Thus the encoder need not reconstruct boundary data that are equivalent for
the requested observables, but it must distinguish every pair that some
admitted geometry makes observably different. Enlarging $\Theta$ can only
increase this requirement. A geometry-conditioned encoder is judged by the
corresponding per-geometry separations; any reduction it achieves comes from
conditioning, not from a universal low-dimensional boundary code.

This yields a three-part scientific scorecard:

| Bottleneck | Irreducible object | Diagnostic question |
|---|---|---|
| Boundary information | Packing complexity of the admissible boundary class under $d_\Theta$ | Do two encoded-identical inputs produce outputs separated by more than the tolerance anywhere in the family? |
| State or output carrier | Linear or nonlinear width of the response family; compare one common carrier with geometry-conditioned carriers | Is the desired response representable before any learned map is considered? |
| Learned map | Description and sample complexity of the map between sufficient input and output coordinates | Once both representations are generous, does accuracy still require rapidly growing model or data complexity? |

Published DeepONet theory already separates encoding, finite-map
approximation, and reconstruction errors
([Lanthaler, Mishra, and Karniadakis, Theorem 3.2](https://academic.oup.com/imatrm/article-pdf/6/1/tnac001/42785544/tnac001.pdf)).
For an affine $p$-dimensional output carrier, its expected reconstruction
error is bounded below by the tail of the output covariance spectrum
(Theorem 3.4). [PCA-Net's Proposition 8](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume24/23-0478/23-0478.pdf)
gives the analogous limitation. These are distributional, affine-carrier
results; the collision bound above is worst-case and architecture-independent,
while nonlinear carriers require their own widths or stable description
complexity.

**EDIT (2026-07-29):** latent dimension alone is not a valid measure of
retained information unless representation class, numerical precision, and
stability are fixed. One real coordinate can hide arbitrarily many bits in
unbounded precision, and an unstable encoder can fold distant inputs together.
The earlier rank-four results still refute the four tested constructions; they
do not establish a lower bound against every four-coordinate nonlinear
representation. This strengthens, rather than changes, the correction in
@sec-nb-transfer-spectrum-state.

Three rival explanations now organize future evidence:

1. **Encoding bottleneck:** family transfer fails because boundary distinctions
   invisible in the training geometries were discarded.
2. **Carrier bottleneck:** each geometry has a compact response space, but
   those spaces rotate enough that one shared carrier is inadequate.
3. **Map bottleneck:** boundary encoding and state capacity are sufficient, but
   the family-dependent map between them is intrinsically hard to learn.

**Research exam, held in reserve.** For each controlled contract expansion,
establish three oracle curves: best task-aware boundary distinction versus
stable information, best fixed and conditioned reconstruction versus carrier
size, and residual model/data scaling after both representations are made
sufficient. At a declared budget, a stage is structurally inadequate if even
its oracle curve exceeds tolerance. For an existing surrogate, a proposed
bottleneck is rejected only when that stage's actual distortion is already
below tolerance while another stage remains above it.

**Decision.** “Generalizable architecture” will mean one whose information,
carrier, and learning costs track the declared task's lower bounds as the
contract expands—not merely one with a fixed latent size. This is an
architecture-level scaling claim; a separate held-out exam is still required
for transfer by one trained model. No experiment or compute is launched during
the research pause.

### Exact ports come before learned states {#sec-nb-exact-ports}

**Agenda result.** Compression should not choose the state. First identify the
exact interface information that makes two adjacent PDE regions composable.
Here, *port* is a unifying name for that information and its admissibility
relation; the underlying literatures call these objects Cauchy data,
Steklov--Poincaré maps, characteristic variables, or scattering operators.

For a second-order elliptic problem on subdomains $\Omega_1$ and $\Omega_2$
sharing $\Gamma$, let $\phi$ be the common Dirichlet trace. Write the outward
conormal flux produced by subdomain $i$ as

$$
q_i(\phi)=q_i^0+\Lambda_i\phi,
$$

where $q_i^0$ is the source-driven flux at zero interface trace and $\Lambda_i$
is the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. Continuity of the solution and balance
of flux give the exact interface equation

$$
(\Lambda_1+\Lambda_2)\phi=-(q_1^0+q_2^0).
$$

Thus $\phi$ is sufficient as an interface *unknown* only because the response
maps carry the eliminated interior physics. Equivalently, the complete port is
the Cauchy pair $(\phi,q)$ constrained to the data space of actual PDE
solutions; its two components are not freely specifiable. This reduction
requires the local boundary problems to be well posed.
[Quarteroni and Valli](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-009-1908-2_14)
derive the corresponding Steklov--Poincaré reduction, while
[Claeys and Hiptmair, Proposition 4.4](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1051/m2an/2012011.pdf)
give a Maxwell example in which a Calderón projector characterizes the
admissible Cauchy-data space.

The exact object changes with the PDE class:

| Problem class | Uncompressed port | Compression implication |
|---|---|---|
| Coercive elliptic or steady diffusion | Primal trace and conjugate flux, or one trace plus a well-posed boundary-response map | Compress only port directions whose transfer decay is established; handle nullspaces and constraints explicitly. |
| Helmholtz or linear waves | Incoming and outgoing characteristic or impedance traces, including every propagating and evanescent channel | Preserve propagating channels; only the transfer-decaying remainder is a compression candidate. Resonance and cutoff limit simple Dirichlet-to-Neumann descriptions. |
